messages.content:
Existing current facts about entities this note mentions:
- memory_id "1000404": On 2025-05-14 the Cinder team observed that webhooks' memory use grew steadily for a week after the cache change.  (about: Cinder, webhooks)
- memory_id "1000387": On 2025-05-07 the Boreal team pinged the owners of the authentication gateway about the error rate.  (about: Boreal team, authentication gateway)
- memory_id "1000384": On 2025-05-07 the Boreal team noticed that the authentication gateway's error rate crept up to 2 percent after the dependency bump.  (about: Boreal team, authentication gateway)
- memory_id "1000364": As of 2025-04-24, the Cinder team reported that the feature-flags service's p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy.  (about: Cinder, feature-flags)
- memory_id "1000343": The product catalog keeps image metadata in a separate table because the joined writes were locking product updates for seconds at a time.  (about: product catalog)
- memory_id "1000321": As of 2025-04-07, the Ember team reported that the notifier's request volume halved after the client rollout.  (about: notifier, Ember team)
- memory_id "1000303" [constraint]: Changes to the billing API need a rollback plan attached to the pull request.  (about: billing API)
- memory_id "1000286": On 2025-03-26 the Dune team observed that the notification service's memory use grew steadily for a week after the cache change.  (about: Dune team, notification service)
- memory_id "1000253": The ledger service relies on the auth gateway for service tokens, so if the auth gateway is down, the ledger service is down.  (about: ledger service, auth gateway)
- memory_id "1000230": On 2025-02-21 the Boreal team pinged the owners of the ledger service about the memory growth.  (about: Boreal team, ledger service)
- memory_id "1000227": On 2025-02-21 the Boreal team noticed that the ledger service's memory use had grown steadily for a week after the cache change.  (about: Boreal team, ledger service)
- memory_id "1000219" [decision]: The notifier will retry failed pushes three times with exponential backoff.  (about: notifier)
- memory_id "1000171" [decision]: Notifier consumers will commit offsets every five seconds.  (about: notifier, notifier consumers)
- memory_id "1000169": The root cause of INC-2025-004 was a consumer offset stuck after a broker restart.  (about: INC-2025-004)
- memory_id "1000165": During incident INC-2025-004, the notifier missed alerts for 40 minutes on 2025-02-01.  (about: notifier, INC-2025-004)
- memory_id "1000160" [constraint]: The ledger service must stay on Postgres 14 until the partitioning work finishes.  (about: ledger service, Postgres 14)
- memory_id "1000149": Oskar runs the weekly architecture review.  (about: Oskar, weekly architecture review)
- memory_id "1000109" [constraint]: The ledger service only ships on weekday mornings before 11:00 UTC.  (about: ledger service)
- memory_id "1000089": The billing API depends on the ledger service for invoice postings.  (about: ledger service, billing API)
- memory_id "1000033": The ledger service is owned by the Atlas team.  (about: Atlas team, ledger service)
Existing entity names: Cinder, webhooks, Boreal team, authentication gateway, feature-flags, product catalog, notifier, Ember team, billing API, Dune team, notification service, ledger service, auth gateway, notifier consumers, INC-2025-004, Postgres 14, Oskar, weekly architecture review, Atlas team

The note:

[2025-05-30] incident-review/INC-2025-011: Review of INC-2025-011 (Ledger, 2025-05-24). The root cause was an index missing after the schema migration. We decided that ledger migrations will ship with a reviewed query plan, because a missing index after a migration caused INC-2025-011.

Durable facts:
1. The root cause of INC-2025-011 was an index missing after the schema migration. (about: INC-2025-011)
2. Decision: Ledger migrations will ship with a reviewed query plan. (about: ledger service)

The note says "Review of INC-2025-011 (Ledger, 2025-05-24)" — the incident affected the ledger service. I could add a relation: src INC-2025-011, dst ledger service, rel_kind "affects" or "incident_of". Hmm, is that inventing? The note says the incident is about Ledger. I think a relation is reasonable: rel_kind "affects" with evidence "Review of INC-2025-011 (Ledger, 2025-05-24)". Or maybe "incident_of". I'll use "affects".

Alias: "Ledger" -> "ledger service". The note uses "Ledger" to refer to the ledger service. Add entity_aliases entry: name "Ledger", canonical "ledger service", evidence "Review of INC-2025-011 (Ledger, 2025-05-24)".

Facts:
- content: "The root cause of INC-2025-011 was an index missing after the schema migration." entities: ["INC-2025-011"]. kind: "fact". confidence: 1. evidence: "The root cause was an index missing after the schema migration."
- content: "Ledger migrations will ship with a reviewed query plan." entities: ["ledger service"]. kind: "decision". evidence: "We decided that ledger migrations will ship with a reviewed query plan". Confidence 1.

Should the decision fact mention INC-2025-011? The decision is because of the incident, but the fact itself is about ledger migrations. Entities: ledger service. Could include INC-2025-011 as entity since the decision is tied to it? The fact sentence "Ledger migrations will ship with a reviewed query plan" is about ledger service. I'll keep entities as ["ledger service"].
